title: URL redirect map — digitallyshifted.com relaunch

platform.production: LiteSpeed on dshost.co.za (Plesk). Apache-compatible .htaccess generated into the build output at deploy time; upload is a DIG-20 go-live step.
platform.staging: GitHub Pages project hosting cannot execute .htaccess. The file ships inert in the staging output; staging routes serve directly under /website-relaunch.

Any category slug not in the explicit list goes to the blog hub, never into a 404. Guards: target must exist (file/dir).

WordPress date archives were never content; intentionally removed.

Any date-structured post URL outside the mapped set (old drafts, comment pages) is gone. Runs after every explicit rule. Guards: skip when the path exists as a file or directory so the pillar guide keeps serving.

Search results have no static equivalent; land on the blog hub.

media.nameRule: Same base name as the old upload; the 12 converted files (jpg/png to webp) use the webp name. Derivation is verified against legacy-static/assets/media at generation time.
media.deployRule: scripts/build-site.sh prunes media that no deploy page references (DIG-90), so the generator emits exact 301s only for files present in the build output. At the current build state that is 2 of 47 (Artboard-10.webp, pexels-ketut-subiyanto-4350093.webp). Analytics.webp lost its last deploy reference when DIG-92 ported the blog index to Astro. Every other old upload URL returns 410 until a page that reuses the asset ships and the file re-enters the output.

steps: Build a production output with scripts/build-site.sh.
Serve the output through the .htaccess rule engine (LiteSpeed-compatible subset) over local HTTP.
Request every old URL, slash and query variants, tag samples, system endpoints, all 47 media URLs and host variants.
Assert status and Location for each case and that every 301 target exists in the build output.
Extract every internal URL from the old-page records and prove each one is covered by the map (no orphans).
verification.hostCaveat: The local test executes the generated .htaccess rules through a compatible engine. A curl pass against the live LiteSpeed host is a DIG-20 go-live step.
